name: Apple macOS
summary: Commercial UNIX-certified operating system developed by Apple for Mac computers, founded on the hybrid XNU kernel, the Darwin foundation and the Apple Silicon hardware architecture.
license: Proprietary commercial (Apple EULA) with open-source Darwin foundation (APSL)

content.introduction: Apple macOS is the proprietary operating system developed by Apple Inc. for its range of Macintosh personal and professional computers (MacBook, iMac, Mac mini, Mac Studio and Mac Pro).
content.what_is_it: Successor of NeXTSTEP and of classic Mac OS (1984-2001), macOS combines a refined graphical interface with a POSIX environment certified UNIX by The Open Group (Single UNIX Specification UNIX 03 standard).
content.kernel_architecture_and_darwin: macOS rests on the open-source Darwin foundation and its hybrid XNU kernel ("X is Not Unix"). The XNU architecture merges two fundamental components: the Mach 3.0 microkernel (responsible for managing tasks, threads, inter-process communication through IPC ports and virtual memory management) and a monolithic layer derived from FreeBSD (providing the POSIX interface, BSD identity and permission management, the TCP/IP network stack and the virtual file system VFS). For hardware support, macOS traditionally used I/O Kit (an object-oriented framework written in restricted C++ in kernel space), progressively replaced by DriverKit, a modern model running hardware drivers in user space in order to immunise the kernel against software panics. Asynchronous task scheduling and system parallelism are orchestrated in depth by Grand Central Dispatch (GCD / libdispatch).
content.hardware_transition_and_graphics: macOS has carried out a major architectural transformation with the transition from Intel x86-64 processors to the proprietary ARM64 Apple Silicon architecture (M1, M2, M3, M4 chips). This platform relies on a unified memory architecture (UMA) allowing the central processor (CPU), the graphics processor (GPU) and the neural engine to share a single physical memory space at very high bandwidth without inter-bus copying. Backwards compatibility with the legacy Intel application catalogue is ensured by the Rosetta 2 binary emulator, combining static AOT (Ahead-Of-Time) translation during installation and dynamic JIT compilation for code generated on the fly. On the display side, Apple has fully deprecated OpenGL and OpenCL in favour of the exclusive use of its low-level Metal graphics API, optimised for direct hardware rendering and intensive computing on its integrated GPUs.
content.storage_integrity_and_security: Storage and security in macOS are organised around the APFS file system (Apple File System) and the SSV (Sealed System Volume) model. Since macOS Big Sur, the system partition containing the whole OS is cryptographically sealed in the form of a SHA-256 hash tree (Merkle tree). At boot, the hardware root of trust (Secure Enclave and Apple Silicon secure boot) validates the cryptographic fingerprint of the sealed volume before authorising its read-only mounting; any attempt at modification outside an official update invalidates the seal and blocks booting. Application security combines system integrity protection (SIP, forbidding even the `root` superuser to modify critical system areas), Gatekeeper (imposing Apple code signing and notarisation of third-party binaries), the application sandbox (App Sandbox) and the TCC system (Transparency, Consent, and Control), which requires every application to ask for the user's explicit consent before accessing private data, the camera or the microphone.
content.ecosystem_continuity_and_limits: macOS shares close technological foundations with iOS, iPadOS, watchOS and visionOS (Darwin kernel, Foundation and CoreGraphics frameworks, Swift language, Quartz Compositor window manager). It nonetheless stands apart through its relative openness: it preserves full access to the UNIX command interpreter (zsh by default), to free development environments (through the Xcode Command Line Tools and community managers such as Homebrew) and allows loading applications distributed outside the official Mac App Store. This integration comes with a strict dependence on Apple hardware: the contractual licence terms forbid running macOS on non-Apple machines (making Hackintosh configurations obsolete and unstable in the face of Apple Silicon security), and the close control exercised by the manufacturer restricts hardware modularity and component upgradability after purchase.
content.origine_et_nomenclature_des_versions: Apple publishes the list of versions of its system with, for each, the last delivered number. The series starts at Mac OS X Cheetah 10.0.4 and continues with Puma 10.1.5, Jaguar 10.2.8, Panther 10.3.9, Tiger 10.4.11, Leopard 10.5.8, Snow Leopard 10.6.8, Lion 10.7.5, Mountain Lion 10.8.5, Mavericks 10.9.5, Yosemite 10.10.5 and El Capitan 10.11.6. The prefix then changes: Sierra 10.12.6, High Sierra 10.13.6 and Mojave 10.14.6 are named macOS, Catalina 10.15.8 closes the 10.x numbering, then the series resumes at 11 with Big Sur 11.7.11, followed by Monterey 12.7.6, Ventura 13.7.8, Sonoma 14.8.9, Sequoia 15.8.1, Tahoe 26 in 26.7.1 and Golden Gate 27 in 27.0.1. The page carrying this list is dated 28 September 2026 and refers, for each major version, to the list of compatible models. The nomenclature is therefore not a simple counter: the move from 10.15 to 11 then from 15 to 26 corresponds to changes of numbering regime, and the commercial version remains attached to a name.
content.canaux_de_mise_a_jour_et_fenetre_de_supp: Updating is covered by three documented mechanisms. The first is the process itself: Apple states that the system verifies the integrity of an update, personalises it for the device and prevents rollback attacks, and that the user data volume is never mounted during the operation. The second is granularity: alongside major versions and patches, background security improvements are delivered separately and their content can be accumulated in the following minor update. The third is deferral: the documentation describes a deferral window of 90 days before an update becomes visible to the user, and distinct battery thresholds according to the type of device and the trigger mode, 50% for an automatic update on a Mac with an Intel processor against 20% for an update started by the user. Updates can be cached on a Mac running macOS 10.13 or later, with content caching enabled, the device nonetheless having to reach Apple's servers to finalise the operation.
content.package_distribution_and_app_control: Apple documents three software distribution paths that are not to be confused. The first is the Mac App Store, which serves only signed and verified applications. The second is the `.pkg` package: a fleet management solution can install packages on supervised Macs, either through the declarative application management available from macOS 26, or through the `InstallEnterpriseApplication` command on any managed Mac; the package must be signed by a signature verifiable by the device, can contain one or more applications and content installed outside `/Applications`, and declarative management allows a package to be marked as required or optional. The third is the application downloaded outside the store, controlled by Gatekeeper, which verifies that the software comes from an identified developer, that it is notarised by Apple and that it has not been modified, with the user's agreement at first launch. XProtect completes the set by identifying and blocking malicious software already present.
content.installation_et_reinstallation_de_macos: System installation is described according to five methods. The first is the update through the System Settings software panel, presented as the most direct because it offers only versions compatible with the machine and requires less space than the other methods. The second is booting from macOS Recovery, used to reinstall the system, when the update fails or when the machine no longer starts for lack of a working system. The third goes through the terminal, which makes it possible to download the installer of a compatible version no older than the one delivered with the machine. The fourth is the creation of a bootable medium. The fifth groups the methods specific to older versions. Each major version is moreover associated with a list of compatible models, published separately: installation is therefore not only a question of method, but also of Mac model recognised for the target version.
advantages: Official UNIX 03 certification offering a complete POSIX environment for software development
Hardware optimisation and energy efficiency on Apple Silicon architectures
Robust multi-layer security architecture (Signed System Volume, SIP, Gatekeeper, Secure Enclave)
Modern APFS file system with local snapshots and zero-cost file cloning
Unified ecosystem and transparent continuity with iOS and iPadOS devices
disadvantages: Contractual and technical lock-in exclusive to physical hardware manufactured by Apple
Source code of the graphical interface, of the Cocoa/SwiftUI frameworks and of the drivers under proprietary licence
Native video game catalogue significantly smaller than on Windows or on Linux with Proton
Growing constraints on running independent software not notarised by Apple servers
who_is_it_for: Software developers, engineers and content creators looking for a stable graphical UNIX environment
Audiovisual, music publishing and graphic creation professionals using the Apple suite
Users with Apple equipment favouring ecosystem integration and simplicity of maintenance
who_is_it_not_for: Users wishing to assemble their own desktop computer or freely change hardware components
Standard computing or server infrastructures requiring ordinary x86-64 virtualisation
Intensive PC gamers depending on a native x86 game catalogue and third-party GPU drivers
content.verdict: Apple macOS is Apple's proprietary operating system for its Macintosh computers. It rests on a POSIX environment certified UNIX 03 by The Open Group, on the XNU kernel and on the Apple Silicon architecture, with an interface and an application ecosystem controlled by Apple.
